_comment: Written by the agent each day (3 EN post ideas for the operator). Keep facts and numbers traceable to posts on the board. Short hyphen only, no new numbers.

ideas.title: Harnesses beat model chasing again
ideas.topic: Open source tools and free access
ideas.hook_en: I used to chase the next big model. Lately I catch myself chasing harnesses instead. Cheap mid-tier models plus a plugin layer people actually enjoy hacking. That feels closer to how we once flashed ROMs than how we buy API tiers. If your agent stack only upgrades models and never upgrades the shell around them, you are optimizing the wrong layer.
ideas.video_tip: 18s screencast: open a blank agent shell, drop in two plugins side by side, flash a caption 'model stays; harness changes' then cut to a tiny plugin list scrolling like an Obsidian community tab.
ideas.angle: yin min as DevOps + Agent builder: platform/shell > raw model upgrades; rides DeepSeek Harness plugin wave without copying anyone's punchline.
ideas.why: op7418's DeepSeek Harness plugin post hit 339K views; vista8's Harness-as-Obsidian take hit 46K. Open-source tooling keywords were heavy on the board.

ideas.title: Stop interviewing for what Claude already owns
ideas.hook_en: If your interview still hinges on a textbook coding puzzle, you are ranking candidates against Claude's homework set. I hire for ops and agents: I care who can debug a flaky retrieval path, own a failure mode, and say no to a shiny memory framework. The race is not who types faster. It is who still has judgment when the model is already fluent.
ideas.video_tip: 12s: whiteboard erase of a leetcode-style prompt, rewrite three bullets: failure ownership, retrieval debugging, shipping judgment; end on 'Claude owns the puzzle; you own the system'.
ideas.angle: Personal hiring/ops judgment reacting to Anthropic skipping classic coding screens — original voice, not a summary of Felix's blog.
ideas.why: dotey's Felix Rieseberg interview piece hit 84K; Anthropic/Claude keywords dominated view-weighted lexicon; Claude-authored ETH paper thread hit 68K.

ideas.title: Personal agents are shipping before enterprise memory is ready
ideas.hook_en: Timeline today: consumer agents plugging into payments and rides, Grok Bot desks running unattended loops, and my own posts still lagging the 5K view bar. That contrast is the story. Distribution for personal agents is accelerating. Durable memory and retrieval for the same agents is still the boring bottleneck. I am not scared of the demos. I am watching who ships the memory layer that does not fall over on day three.
ideas.video_tip: 15s split: left a personal-agent home screen lighting up connectors; right a RAG trace with a red 'day-3 forgotten context' flash; caption 'ship the connector last if memory is still soft'.
ideas.angle: Rides personal-Agent + Grok Bot wave while anchoring yin min's RAG/Memory lane and honest self-performance vs thresholds.
ideas.why: xiaohu's personal Agent / 灵光 2.0 post hit 43K; 0xlangeai's Grok Bot quant video hit 128K; board keywords topped with Claude/Anthropic then AI Agent / Grok Bot.
